newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-SPORTING LISBON BOOED BY FANS DESPITE VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPORTING LISBON BOOED BY FANS DESPITE VICTORY.

text.p: Fans of Sporting Lisbon whistled their disappointment at the team's performance despite a 2-0 win over Gil Vicente on Sunday.
Reigning champions Porto, apparently oblivious to corruption allegations hanging over the club, stayed top of the table following their 1-0 win away over Rio Ave on Friday.
Porto have 26 points, followed by Benfica with 23 and Sporting with 22.
Sporting scored their opening goal against Gil Vicente in the 11th minute with a close-range shot by Nigerian striker Emmanuel Amunike as players from both teams piled into the box.

Gil Vicente, last-but-one in the first division, complained to the referee that their goalkeeper, Croatian Vatroslav Mihacic, had been fouled by Sporting's Moroccan midfielder Mustapha Hadji. But their protests were ignored.
Ivorian striker Ahmed Ouattara made it 2-0 for lacklustre Sporting with a powerful shot in injury time.
Porto's Brazilian striker Mario Jardel secured his team's victory against Rio Ave with a header inside the box from a pass by compatriot Aloisio Alves eight minutes from the final whistle.
Jardel has scored several match-winning goals for Porto in both European and domestic matches this season.

Porto, who have already qualified for the last eight of the European Cup, face AC Milan at home in the Champions' League section of the competition on Wednesday. They need just one point to finish top of Group D of the Champions' League.

Porto are caught in the middle of a crisis over alleged corruption in Portuguese soccer, with the most serious case involving accusations that the team sought to bribe a referee ahead of a European match against Aberdeen 12 years ago. Porto have denied any bribery attempt was made.

On Saturday, an early goal by Bulgarian midfielder Ilian Iliev opened the way for Benfica's 3-0 win away against newly-promoted Espinho, scoring in the 10th minute from a fine pass by Brazilian striker Hassan Donizete.
Espinho, the surprise of the season, are joint fourth in the championship. They had three excellent chances but failed to score.
Benfica's Belgian goalkeeper Michel Preud'homme made spectacular saves to deflect two shots for corners and Espinho's Brazilian midfielder Marco Luis hit the bar with a free-kick in the 76th minute.

Benfica scored their second goal with a free-kick by Brazilian Valdo Filho in the 86th minute. Substitute Luis Gustavo scored with a powerful shot from outside the area to seal the win in the last minute.
